24 import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner; 25 26 /** 27 * Repository class for Owner domain objects All method names are compliant with Spring Data naming 28 * conventions so this interface can easily be extended for Spring Data See here: http://static.springsource.org/spring-data/jpa/docs/current/reference/html/jpa.repositories.html#jpa.query-methods.query-creation 29 * 30 * @author Ken Krebs 31 * @author Juergen Hoeller 32 * @author Sam Brannen 33 * @author Michael Isvy 34 * @author Vitaliy Fedoriv 35 */ 36 public interface OwnerRepository { 37 38 /** 39 * Retrieve Owners from the data store by last name, returning all owners whose last name starts 40 * with the given name. 41 * 42 * @param lastName Value to search for 43 * @return a Collection of matching Owners (or an empty Collection if none 44 * found) 45 */ 46 Collection findByLastName(String lastName) throws DataAccessException; 47 48 Page findByLastName(String lastName, Pageable pageable) throws DataAccessException; 49 50 /** 51 * Report whether any Owner already uses the given (already normalized) telephone number. 52 * 53 * @param telephone the normalized telephone number to check for 54 * @return true if at least one Owner has this telephone, false otherwise 55 */ 56 boolean existsByTelephone(String telephone) throws DataAccessException; 57 58 /** 59 * Retrieve an Owner from the data store by id. 60 * 61 * @param id the id to search for 62 * @return the Owner if found 63 * @throws org.springframework.dao.DataRetrievalFailureException if not found 64 */ 65 Owner findById(int id) throws DataAccessException; 66 67 68 /** 69 * Save an Owner to the data store, either inserting or updating it. 70 * 71 * @param owner the Owner to save 72 * @see BaseEntity#isNew 73 */ 74 void save(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException; 75 76 /** 77 * Retrieve Owners from the data store, returning all owners 78 * 79 * @return a Collection of Owners (or an empty Collection if none 80 * found) 81 */ 82 Collection findAll() throws DataAccessException; 83 84 Page findAll(Pageable pageable) throws DataAccessException; 85 86 /** 87 * Delete an Owner to the data store by Owner. 88 * 89 * @param owner the Owner to delete 90 * 91 */ 92 void delete(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException; content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The feature is wired coherently (model field, mapper ignores, schema across all four DBs, controller header handling, service + interface method) — all additive and idiomatic except for one placement/idiom problem:

**`findOwnerByIdempotencyKey` does the lookup in the wrong unit, bypassing the repository.** In `ClinicServiceImpl` the method loads *every* owner via `ownerRepository.findAll().stream()` and filters in memory:

```java
return ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
    .filter(existing -> !existing.isDeleted())
    .filter(existing -> idempotencyKey.equals(existing.getIdempotencyKey()))
    .findFirst()
    .orElse(null);
```

This is not how lookups are done in this codebase. `OwnerRepository` is a Spring Data–style repository whose own javadoc states "All method names are compliant with Spring Data naming conventions," and existing single-attribute lookups are expressed as derived query methods there — `findByLastName(...)`, `existsByTelephone(...)`, `findById(...)`. A by-key lookup belongs in the same place, not as a full-table scan filtered in the service layer.

Concrete change:
- Add a query method to `OwnerRepository`, e.g. `Owner findByIdempotencyKey(String idempotencyKey) throws DataAccessException;` (mirroring `existsByTelephone` / `findByLastName`), and implement it in the repository implementation like the other derived methods.
- Have `ClinicServiceImpl.findOwnerByIdempotencyKey` simply delegate to it (keeping the null/blank guard), so the service orchestrates and the persistence concern stays in the repository. This also removes the `findAll()`-and-filter pattern that no other lookup in this service uses.

Minor (optional, not blocking): the controller computes `idempotencyKey != null && !idempotencyKey.isBlank()` twice in `addOwner`; a single local boolean would read more cleanly, though it's acceptable as-is.
